title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, team wiki
author: Daniel Kim
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical platform engineering landing doc for systems and services, dashboards & alerts, runbooks, retrospectives, the near-term roadmap, and the team wiki structure. It consolidates ownership, operational standards, and how‑tos for common platform tasks so oncall, SRE, and platform engineers can act quickly and consistently.

Scope

- Applies to all services managed by eng-platform (control plane, provisioning, observability, autoscaling, multi‑cluster routing).
- Excludes model-serving runtime internals (see eng-serving-runtime).

Systems & services inventory (high level)

Service | Purpose | Primary Owner | SLOs
--------|---------|---------------|------
platform-control-plane | API surface for routing/tenancy | platform-api@redwood.com | 99.95% availability, p95 latency < 120ms
provisioner | Provision Dedicated/private clusters | infra-provisioning@redwood.com | 99.9% availability, p95 job completion < 60s
telemetry-collector | Ingest metrics/traces/logs | observability@redwood.com | 99.9% availability, 1m ingest lag SLA
autoscaler | Global autoscaling policy engine | platform-scaling@redwood.com | Scale decisions within 30s target
auth-gateway | RBAC and token validation | security@redwood.com | 99.99% availability, p99 auth latency < 50ms

Each service page (links in team wiki) must include: API endpoints, health endpoints, runbooks, dashboards, alert lists, owners, and rollout checklist. See "Team wiki structure" below.

Dashboards & Alerts

Dashboard naming convention:
- platform.<service>.<view> (e.g. platform.provisioner.overview, platform.telemetry-ingest.errors)
- Each dashboard includes: owner, last updated date, purpose, and key panels (SLO, errors, latency, capacity).

Key dashboards to check during incidents:
1) platform.control-plane.overview: total requests, 5xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, backpressure queue depth.
2) platform.provisioner.jobs: jobs pending, avg completion time, failure rate by image.
3) observability.ingest.pipeline: input throughput, processing lag, secondary queue length.
4) platform.autoscaler.decisions: node counts, pending scale ops, policy rejections.

Alerting standards (owner: observability team)
- All alerts must include: symptom, impact, runbook link, severity (P1/P2/P3), owner, and suggested remediation steps.
- Use grouping to avoid pager noise: group by service and cluster for noisy signals.
- Default severities:
  - P1: Service-level SLO breach risk or customer-visible outage
  - P2: Functional degradation with workaround
  - P3: Low-priority errors or growth signals

Example Prometheus alert expressions:
- High 95th latency (P2):
  ALERT: PlatformControlPlaneHighLatency
  IF histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.12
  FOR 5m
  ANNOTATIONS: summary="p95 latency >120ms", runbook="confluence/eng-platform/platform-control-plane-runbook-2026.json"

- Telemetry ingestion backpressure (P1):
  ALERT: TelemetryIngestQueueGrowing
  IF increase(telemetry_queue_length[10m]) > 1000
  FOR 3m
  ANNOTATIONS: summary="backlog growing >1000 in 10m", runbook="confluence/eng-platform/observability-ingest-runbook-2026.json"

Alert lifecycle requirements:
- Every alert must have an owner (team alias) and a playbook link.
- On alert creation reviewers must confirm severity and runbook.
- Disable alerts if they are noisy or trigger due to planned maintenance. Use the alert-snooze tool and document the change.

Runbooks (short & actionable)

Platform P1 incident runbook (high level)
1) Triage (0-5 min): Confirm P1 using dashboards, post incident on #status and create incident in Incident Manager.
2) Notify (5 min): PagerDuty P1 run; send initial update to exec-incident channel.
3) Contain (5-20 min): Route traffic to fallback model variants or standby region; enable autoscaler emergency override if capacity related.
4) Mitigate (20-60 min): Apply configuration rollback or scale up reserved pools; restart affected pods/services behind feature flags.
5) Restore & verify (60-120 min): Verify SLOs, run smoke tests, and confirm with customers if externally visible.
6) Postmortem (within 48h): Assign incident owner for full postmortem and action item tracking.

Common quick fixes (copyable commands)
- Restart failed provisioner jobs on cluster-x:
  kubectl -n provisioner get jobs | grep Failed | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 kubectl -n provisioner delete job
- Temporarily increase control-plane replicas:
  kubectl -n platform scale deployment control-plane --replicas=6
- Force flush telemetry pipeline:
  curl -X POST "https://telemetry.internal/_admin/flush" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

How‑tos (step-by-step)

How to add a new dashboard:
1) Create dashboard with name platform.<service>.<view> in Grafana.
2) Add panels for: SLO, error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), traffic, and capacity.
3) Document purpose, owner, and update timestamp in the dashboard description.
4) Open PR to add dashboard id to team wiki inventory and link runbook.
5) Reviewer checklist: verify panels, thresholds, and annotation for deploys.

How to onboard a new service to platform monitoring:
1) Define SLOs with product/eng owner.
2) Add metrics (request_total, request_errors, latency histogram).
3) Create dashboards and corresponding alerts.
4) Add runbook and escalation policy.
5) Run a 7-day monitoring burn-in before moving to production.

Retrospective: Feb 2026 telemetry ingest incident (summary)

Summary:
- Date: 2026-01-28
- Impact: 2-hour degraded telemetry ingestion leading to delayed observability for two customer accounts.
- Root cause: sudden spike in malformed events that caused prolonged CPU GC in collector workers; backpressure policy incorrectly throttled healthy traffic.

Action items (status):
- Fix input validation to drop malformed events earlier (owner: observability) — completed 2026-02-05.
- Increase default collector heap and add GC tuning (owner: observability) — completed 2026-02-03.
- Add alert for sustained increase in malformed_event_count (owner: observability) — in_review.
- Update backpressure policy to avoid throttling healthy traffic under high error conditions (owner: platform-scaling) — scheduled for 2026-03.

Roadmap (next 6 months)

Q2 2026 priorities:
- Centralize dashboard templates and enforce via dashboard CI (owner: observability).
- Implement autoscaler dry-run mode for policy validation (owner: platform-scaling).
- Add per-tenant cost telemetry to dashboards (owner: billing-infra).
- Ship runbook authoring tool integration to confluence for live playbooks (owner: eng-platform).

Q3 2026 goals (planning):
- Cross-region playbooks and cutover automation for regional outages.
- Observability cost controls with sampling policies and cold storage lifecycle.

Team wiki structure (required pages)
- platform/team-home (this landing doc)
- platform/services/<service-name> (service page with API, runbook, dashboards)
- platform/dashboards/inventory (list of dashboards + owners)
- platform/alerts/catalog (alert definitions and runbook links)
- platform/runbooks/p1, platform/runbooks/p2 (canonical templates)
- platform/roadmap (quarterly goals and milestones)

Ownership & contact points
- Oncall channel: #oncall-platform (primary)
- PagerDuty: Redwood Platform P0/P1 escalation policy
- Slack escalation leads: platform-oncall-leads@redwood.com
- Pager duty schedule owners must keep schedules current and add a secondary for leave periods.

Related resources
- Platform playbook (detailed): confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026.json
- Observability runbook: confluence/eng-platform/observability-ingest-runbook-2026.json
- Incident postmortems archive: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems
